4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the Petitioner is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this case due to some civil dispute.

sentences.text:
In Vijayan v. State of Kerla reported in 2010 SCC 389, the Supreme Court has formulated the following seven guiding principles on discharge and framing of charge:
"(i) The Judge while considering the question of framing of charge under Sec. 227 of Cr.P.C has undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding of whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.

entities.text: Vijayan v. State of Kerla reported in 2010 SCC 389
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To determine prima facie case would depend upon the facts of each case.

(ii) Where the materials placed before the court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been 'properly explained, the court will be fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.

(iii) The court cannot act merely as a post office or a mouth piece of the prosecution,
but it has to consider the broad probabilities of the case.
Location: High Court of Orissa cuttack Date: 27-Feb-2024 11:30:32
There cannot be a roving inquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if the trial being conducted.
(iv) On the basis of material on record if the court could form an opinion that the accused might have committed the offence it can frame the charge.

(v) At the time of framing of the charge the probative value of material on record cannot be gone into but before framing of charge the court must apply its judicial mind on the material placed on record and must be satisfied that the commission by the accused was possible.
(vi) At the stage of Sec. 227 and 228 of the Cr.P.C. the court is required to evaluate the materials and documents on record with a view to find out the existence of all the ingredients considering the alleged offences, but court cannot be expected to presume that the prosecution story is gospel truth.
(vii) if two views are possible one of them gives rise to suspicion only as distinguished from grave suspicion, the trial judge will be empowered to dis-charge the accused irrespective of the result of the trial."
7.

Further in Sajan Kumar v. C.B.I reported in 2010 SCC 368, the Supreme Court has settled the law that at the stage of framing of charge under Section 228 Cr.P.C. or while considering the discharge petition filed under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. it is not for judge concerned to analyses all the materials including Pros and Cons, reliability or acceptability etc. of the evidence.
